questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Development: Meaning and Principles' refers to.
questions.a: Development is the pattern of orderly, sequential change that continues through life -- gains and losses alike -- from conception to old age. Its principles: development proceeds in definite directions, at individual rates, in interrelated dimensions, and through the joint action of heredity and environment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Development: Meaning and Principles'.
questions.a: Lifelong, orderly and joint-made -- development is change with a pattern, not a race with a finish line.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Heredity, Environment and Context' refers to.
questions.a: The nature-nurture issue asks how much genes and how much environment shape us. Developmental psychology answers: jointly -- genes set ranges, environments select points within them, and cultural context colours every stage's meaning and timetable.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Heredity, Environment and Context'.
questions.a: Genes write in pencil, environment fills the ink -- context decides what each stage means.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Heredity, Environment and Context' taught, and from which source text?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Stages of the Life Span' refers to.
questions.a: The life span divides into stages -- prenatal, infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age -- each with characteristic physical, cognitive and socio-emotional tasks, from attachment and language in infancy to identity in adolescence and integrity in old age.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Stages of the Life Span'.
questions.a: One life span, several stages -- each with its own jobs of growth to finish before the next begins.
